questions.q: Kaziranga National Park in Assam holds about what share of the world’s one-horned rhinos?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga holds about two-thirds of the world’s one-horned rhinos and has the highest tiger density.

questions.q: Manas National Park, a UNESCO site in Assam, lies on the border with which country?
questions.explanation: Manas is a UNESCO site on the Bhutan border.

questions.q: Which Assam national park is called ‘mini Kaziranga’?
questions.explanation: Orang (Rajiv Gandhi) National Park is known as ‘mini Kaziranga’.

questions.q: Orang National Park in Assam is also known as:
questions.explanation: Orang is also called Rajiv Gandhi National Park.

questions.q: Nameri National Park in Assam is known for:
questions.explanation: Nameri is known for river rafting and elephants.

questions.q: Dibru-Saikhowa, a riverine national park in Assam, is known for which animals?
questions.explanation: Dibru-Saikhowa is a riverine park known for its feral horses.

questions.q: Which Assam national park is called the ‘Amazon of the East’?
questions.explanation: Dehing Patkai (notified 2021) is a rainforest called the ‘Amazon of the East’.

questions.q: Raimona National Park in Bodoland, Assam, is known for which animal?
questions.explanation: Raimona (notified 2021) is in Bodoland and known for the golden langur.

questions.q: Which is Assam’s newest (8th) national park, notified in 2025?
questions.explanation: Sikhna Jwhwlao, in Bodoland, was notified in 2025 as Assam’s 8th national park.

questions.q: Raimona and Dehing Patkai were notified as national parks in which year?
questions.explanation: Both are marked NEW 2021 in the syllabus.

questions.q: How many national parks does Assam have?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga, Manas, Orang, Nameri, Dibru-Saikhowa, Raimona, Dehing Patkai and Sikhna Jwhwlao: 8 parks.

questions.q: Namdapha is the only park in India with all four big cats. Which animal is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: Namdapha’s four big cats are the tiger, leopard, clouded leopard and snow leopard.

questions.q: Namdapha National Park is in which state?
questions.explanation: Namdapha is in Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.q: Mouling National Park of Arunachal Pradesh lies in which hills?
questions.explanation: Mouling is in the Siang hills.

questions.q: Which are Arunachal Pradesh’s two national parks?
questions.explanation: Arunachal Pradesh has Namdapha and Mouling (‘Morning News’).

questions.q: Keibul Lamjao, the world’s only floating national park, rests on the phumdis of which lake?
questions.explanation: Keibul Lamjao floats on the phumdis of Loktak lake, Manipur.

questions.q: Keibul Lamjao is the home of which deer?
questions.explanation: The Sangai, Manipur’s dancing deer, lives in Keibul Lamjao.

questions.q: Shirui National Park of Manipur is named after:
options: The Shirui lily, Manipur’s state flower
questions.explanation: Shirui’s hills are home to the Shirui lily, the state flower.

questions.q: Which Meghalaya national park is called the ‘land of perpetual winds’?
questions.explanation: Balphakram, sacred to the Garos, is the ‘land of perpetual winds’.

questions.q: Balphakram National Park is sacred to which community?
questions.explanation: Balphakram is sacred to the Garo people.

questions.q: Which Meghalaya national park is also a UNESCO biosphere reserve, known for its citrus gene pool?
questions.explanation: Nokrek is both a national park and a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

questions.q: Which Mizoram national park is known as the ‘Blue Mountain’?
questions.explanation: Phawngpui, the ‘Blue Mountain’, is Mizoram’s highest point.

questions.q: Phawngpui National Park is known for which animals?
questions.explanation: Serow and hoolock gibbon are the key wildlife of Phawngpui.

questions.q: Murlen National Park of Mizoram lies near the border with:
questions.explanation: Murlen is near the Myanmar border.

questions.q: Intanki (Ntangki), Nagaland’s only national park, is known for which animal?
questions.explanation: Intanki is hoolock gibbon country (‘In-Tank-i’).

questions.q: In which year did Khangchendzonga become India’s first ‘mixed’ UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.explanation: Khangchendzonga became India’s first mixed (natural + cultural) World Heritage Site in 2016.

questions.q: Sikkim’s only national park, which is also a biosphere reserve with the world’s 3rd highest peak, is:
questions.explanation: Khangchendzonga is ‘3-in-1’: national park + biosphere + the world’s 3rd highest peak.

questions.q: Which are Tripura’s two national parks?
questions.explanation: Tripura names its parks after the animals in them: Bison (Rajbari) and Clouded Leopard.

questions.q: Bison National Park of Tripura is also called:
questions.explanation: Bison National Park is also known as Rajbari.

questions.q: Which pair of national park and state is INCORRECTLY matched?
questions.explanation: Intanki (Ntangki) is in Nagaland. Mizoram’s parks are Murlen and Phawngpui.

quizzes.subtitle: Andaman & Nicobar, East and the Gangetic plains

questions.q: Which is India’s smallest national park?
questions.explanation: South Button Island in Andaman & Nicobar is India’s smallest national park, about 0.03 sq km.

questions.q: What is the area of South Button Island National Park?
questions.explanation: South Button Island covers just 0.03 sq km.

questions.q: How many national parks does Andaman & Nicobar have, the most of any Union Territory?
questions.explanation: A&N has 9 national parks, the most of any UT.

questions.q: Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park, known for coral reefs, is at:
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park is also called Wandoor.

questions.q: Rani Jhansi Marine National Park lies around which islands?
questions.explanation: Rani Jhansi Marine National Park is around the Ross-Smith islands.

questions.q: Mount Harriet National Park in Andaman & Nicobar has been renamed:
questions.explanation: Mount Harriet is now ‘Mount Manipur’.

questions.q: Saddle Peak National Park is known for:
questions.explanation: Saddle Peak is the highest point of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

questions.q: Galathea National Park on Great Nicobar is known for:
questions.explanation: Galathea is known for leatherback turtles.

questions.q: Which national park lies on Great Nicobar beside Galathea?
questions.explanation: Campbell Bay and Galathea are both on Great Nicobar.

questions.q: Which are the two marine national parks of Andaman & Nicobar?
questions.explanation: The two marine parks are Mahatma Gandhi (Wandoor) and Rani Jhansi.

questions.q: North Button, Middle Button and South Button Island national parks are in:
questions.explanation: The three Button Island parks are in Andaman & Nicobar.

questions.q: Sundarbans National Park is the world’s largest:
questions.explanation: Sundarbans is the world’s largest tidal mangrove forest and a UNESCO site.

questions.q: Which West Bengal park is a UNESCO site known for its mangrove tigers?
questions.explanation: Sundarbans is home to the mangrove tiger.

questions.q: Buxa National Park is linked to:
options: The old fort route to Bhutan
questions.explanation: Buxa is on the old fort route to Bhutan.

questions.q: Which two West Bengal national parks are known for the one-horned rhino?
questions.explanation: Gorumara and Jaldapara are West Bengal’s two rhino parks.

questions.q: Singalila National Park lies on which trek trail?
questions.explanation: Singalila, a red panda park, is on the Sandakphu trail.

questions.q: Neora Valley and Singalila national parks are both known for which animal?
questions.explanation: Both are West Bengal’s red panda hill parks.

questions.q: How many national parks does West Bengal have?
questions.explanation: Sundarbans, Buxa, Gorumara, Jaldapara, Neora Valley and Singalila: 6 parks (‘2-2-1-1’).

questions.q: In which month and year was Similipal formally notified as a national park?
questions.explanation: Similipal was formally notified as a national park only in April 2025.

questions.q: After its 2025 notification, Similipal became India’s ___ national park.
questions.explanation: Similipal became India’s 107th national park.

questions.q: Which Odisha national park is known for tigers, orchids and melanistic tigers?
questions.explanation: Similipal is known for tigers, orchids and melanistic (dark) tigers.

questions.q: Bhitarkanika National Park in Odisha is known for:
questions.explanation: Bhitarkanika’s mangrove creeks hold saltwater crocodiles.

questions.q: Betla National Park in Jharkhand is also known as:
questions.explanation: Betla is the old Palamau.

questions.q: Betla (Palamau) was one of India’s first 9 Project Tiger reserves, set up in which year?
questions.explanation: Betla was among the first 9 Project Tiger reserves in 1973.

questions.q: Which is Jharkhand’s only national park?
questions.explanation: Betla (Palamau) is Jharkhand’s single park.

questions.q: Valmiki National Park lies on the Nepal border along which river?
questions.explanation: Valmiki is on the Nepal border, along the Gandak river.

questions.q: Valmiki is the only national park of which state?
questions.explanation: Valmiki is Bihar’s only national park.

questions.q: Dudhwa National Park is known for the revival of which animal?
questions.explanation: Dudhwa is known for the barasingha (swamp deer) revival.

questions.q: Dudhwa National Park lies on which river?
questions.explanation: Dudhwa is on the Sharda river, on the Indo-Nepal border.

questions.q: Which is Uttar Pradesh’s only national park?
questions.explanation: Dudhwa is UP’s only national park (‘UP gives Doodh’).

questions.q: Which is India’s largest national park?
questions.explanation: Hemis in Ladakh is India’s largest national park, 3,350 sq km.

questions.q: What is the area of Hemis National Park?
questions.explanation: Hemis covers 3,350 sq km.

questions.q: Hemis National Park is known as the capital of which animal?
questions.explanation: Hemis is the ‘snow leopard capital’; it also has the Tibetan wolf and bharal.

questions.q: Dachigam National Park in Jammu & Kashmir is the home of:
questions.explanation: Dachigam is the home of the hangul, or Kashmir stag.

questions.q: Salim Ali National Park in Srinagar is also called:
questions.explanation: Salim Ali NP, named after the birdman of India, is also called City Forest NP.

questions.q: Kazinag National Park in north Kashmir lies on which river?
questions.explanation: Kazinag is in north Kashmir, on the Jhelum.

questions.q: Which Jammu & Kashmir national park is high-altitude snow leopard country?
questions.explanation: Kishtwar is a high-altitude park and snow leopard country.

questions.q: India’s first national park, Jim Corbett, was set up in 1936 under which name?
questions.explanation: Jim Corbett began in 1936 as Hailey National Park.

questions.q: Jim Corbett was also India’s first Project Tiger reserve, in which year?
questions.explanation: Corbett became the first Project Tiger reserve in 1973.

questions.q: Which two Uttarakhand national parks are UNESCO sites?
options: Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers
questions.explanation: Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers are UNESCO sites.

questions.q: Rajaji National Park, known for elephants, is near which town?
questions.explanation: Rajaji is near Haridwar.

questions.q: Govind National Park in Uttarakhand is also known as:
questions.explanation: Govind (Pashu Vihar) is a snow leopard habitat.

questions.q: Which Uttarakhand national park covers the source region of the Ganga?
questions.explanation: Gangotri NP covers the source region of the Ganga.

questions.q: In which year did Great Himalayan National Park become a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
questions.explanation: Great Himalayan NP was inscribed in 2014.

questions.q: Which Himachal Pradesh national park is a cold desert with snow leopards?
questions.explanation: Pin Valley is a cold-desert park with snow leopards.

questions.q: Khirganga National Park is known for the hot springs of which valley?
questions.explanation: Khirganga is known for the Parvati valley hot springs.

questions.q: Which Himachal Pradesh national park is a sal forest in the south of the state?
questions.explanation: Simbalbara is a sal forest in southern Himachal.

questions.q: Which Haryana national park is also a bird sanctuary and a Ramsar site?
questions.explanation: Sultanpur holds three badges: national park, bird sanctuary and Ramsar site.

questions.q: Kalesar National Park, a sal forest in Haryana, lies on which river?
questions.explanation: Kalesar is a sal forest on the Yamuna.

questions.q: Which Rajasthan park is a national park, a UNESCO site and a Ramsar site?
questions.explanation: Keoladeo (Ghana) is known for birds and carries all three badges.

questions.q: Desert National Park near Jaisalmer is known for which bird?
questions.explanation: Desert NP is home to the great Indian bustard.

questions.q: Mukundra Hills National Park is in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Mukundra Hills is in Kota; Sariska is in Alwar.

questions.q: Gir National Park is the only wild home of which animal?
questions.explanation: Gir is the only wild home of the Asiatic lion.

questions.q: Which is India’s first marine national park?
options: Marine National Park, Gulf of Kachchh
Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park
questions.explanation: The Marine National Park in the Gulf of Kachchh, Gujarat, is India’s first.

questions.q: Velavadar National Park in Gujarat is famous for which animal?
questions.explanation: Velavadar is the Blackbuck National Park.

questions.q: Vansda National Park in Gujarat lies in which forest?
questions.explanation: Vansda is a dense Dang forest.

questions.q: Dudhsagar Falls lies inside which national park?
questions.explanation: Bhagwan Mahavir (Mollem), Goa’s only national park, contains Dudhsagar Falls.

questions.q: Which is Maharashtra’s oldest national park (1955)?
questions.explanation: Tadoba, famous for tigers, is the state’s oldest (1955).

questions.q: Sanjay Gandhi (Borivali) National Park lies inside which city?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Gandhi NP is inside Mumbai, one of the world’s few city national parks.

questions.q: Gugamal National Park of Maharashtra is part of which tiger reserve?
questions.explanation: Gugamal is in the Melghat tiger reserve.

questions.q: Which state has the most national parks, with 11?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh has 11 national parks (‘MP = 11 pandits’).

questions.q: Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh is the home of which deer?
questions.explanation: Kanha is the barasingha’s home.

questions.q: Which Madhya Pradesh national park is the origin of the white tiger?
questions.explanation: Bandhavgarh is the origin of the white tiger.

questions.q: Kuno National Park is the new home of which animal?
questions.explanation: Kuno is the cheetah’s new home.

questions.q: Panna National Park lies on which river?
questions.explanation: Panna is on the Ken river.

questions.q: Which two Madhya Pradesh national parks are fossil parks?
options: Dinosaur Fossils and Mandla Plant Fossils
questions.explanation: MP’s 11 include 2 fossil parks: Dinosaur Fossils and Mandla Plant Fossils.

questions.q: Madhav National Park is at:
questions.explanation: Madhav National Park is in Shivpuri.

questions.q: Van Vihar National Park is:
questions.explanation: Van Vihar is a zoo-park inside Bhopal.

questions.q: Pench National Park of Madhya Pradesh shares a border with which state?
questions.explanation: Pench lies on the MP-Maharashtra border; Maharashtra’s side is Pench (Jawaharlal Nehru).

questions.q: Which five Madhya Pradesh parks are the ‘tiger giants’ (K.B.P.P.S.)?
options: Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Van Vihar, Panna, Sanjay
questions.explanation: The memory trick groups Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench, Panna and Satpura as the 5 tiger giants.

questions.q: Kanger Valley (Ghati) National Park in Chhattisgarh is famous for:
options: Caves and the Bastar hill myna
questions.explanation: Kanger Valley is famous for its caves and the Bastar hill myna, the state bird.

questions.q: Guru Ghasidas National Park, the largest park of Chhattisgarh, was earlier called:
questions.explanation: Guru Ghasidas is the erstwhile Sanjay NP.

questions.q: Sri Venkateswara National Park in Andhra Pradesh lies in which hills?
questions.explanation: Sri Venkateswara is in the Tirupati hills and is known for the tiger.

questions.q: Papikonda National Park of Andhra Pradesh lies along which river gorge?
questions.explanation: Papikonda is in the Godavari gorge.

questions.q: Rajiv Gandhi (Rameswaram) National Park, one of India’s tiniest, lies on which river?
questions.explanation: It covers about 2.4 sq km on the Penna; don’t confuse it with Assam’s or Karnataka’s Rajiv Gandhi NP.

questions.q: What does ‘KBR’ stand for in KBR National Park, Hyderabad?
questions.explanation: KBR is Kasu Brahmananda Reddy National Park, inside Hyderabad city.

questions.q: Mrugavani National Park, a deer park in Telangana, is at:
questions.explanation: Mrugavani is a deer park at Chilkur.

questions.q: All three national parks of Telangana are in or near which city?
questions.explanation: KBR, Mahavir Harina Vanasthali and Mrugavani are all Hyderabad parks.

questions.q: Guindy National Park lies inside which metro city?
questions.explanation: Guindy is a national park inside Chennai.

questions.q: Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park is known for:
questions.explanation: Gulf of Mannar is known for dugongs and corals.

questions.q: Indira Gandhi National Park of Tamil Nadu is also known as:
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi NP is Annamalai, with Topslip.

questions.q: Which pair of national parks are both known for the Nilgiri tahr?
questions.explanation: Mukurthi (Tamil Nadu) and Eravikulam (Kerala) are Nilgiri tahr parks.

questions.q: Mudumalai National Park of Tamil Nadu lies on the border with which state?
questions.explanation: Mudumalai is on the Karnataka border.

questions.q: Silent Valley National Park in Kerala is known for which animal?
questions.explanation: Silent Valley is known for the lion-tailed macaque.

questions.q: Periyar National Park in Kerala is known for:
questions.explanation: Periyar has an artificial lake and elephants.

questions.q: Which three are Kerala’s Shola national parks?
questions.explanation: Kerala’s 6 = ‘PES’ (Periyar, Eravikulam, Silent Valley) + a ‘MAP’ of 3 Sholas.

questions.q: Kudremukh National Park in Karnataka is named after:
questions.explanation: Kudremukh means horse-face; the park is named after the peak.

questions.q: Nagarahole National Park in Karnataka is also known as:
questions.explanation: Nagarahole is also called Rajiv Gandhi NP and is known for elephants and leopards.

questions.q: Bandipur and Nagarahole lie in which biosphere reserve, India’s first?
questions.explanation: Both are in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, India’s first.

questions.q: Anshi National Park in Karnataka is part of which tiger reserve?
questions.explanation: Anshi is part of the Kali tiger reserve; Bannerghatta is Bengaluru’s own park.

questions.q: What is the name of the strategic 14.15-kilometer twin-tube all-weather road tunnel connecting Srinagar and Leh, constructed beneath the Zojila Pass?
questions.explanation: The Zojila Tunnel beneath the Zojila Pass (at 11,578 ft elevation) links Baltal and Minamarg on NH-1, cutting travel time across the pass from over 3 hours to approximately 15–20 minutes with year-round military and civilian transit.

questions.q: Which launch vehicle of ISRO successfully launched Chandrayaan-3 into translunar orbit prior to its historic soft landing near the lunar south pole?
questions.explanation: ISRO's heavy-lift LVM3-M4 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3, nicknamed 'Fat Boy') launched Chandrayaan-3 from SDSC SHAR Sriharikota on July 14, 2023, preceding the Vikram lander's touchdown on August 23, 2023.

questions.q: Under the PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, how many households are targeted to receive rooftop solar systems offering up to 300 units of free power each month?
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved the PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana with an outlay of ₹75,021 crore to install rooftop solar panels for 1 crore households, giving up to 300 units of free electricity every month.

questions.q: Under the PM-eBus Sewa initiative approved by the Union Cabinet, how many electric buses will be deployed across Indian cities on a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model?
questions.explanation: PM-eBus Sewa aims to augment green city bus operations by deploying 10,000 electric buses across cities with populations of 3 to 40 lakh, supported by central government subsidies for 10 years.

questions.q: The PM Vishwakarma Scheme provides holistic end-to-end support, subsidized credit of up to ₹3 lakh, and modern toolkit incentives for traditional artisans across how many recognized trades?
questions.explanation: The PM Vishwakarma scheme covers 18 traditional family-based crafts (including carpenters, blacksmiths, potters, sculptors, and cobblers) with ₹13,000 crore budgetary allocation.

questions.q: Who were jointly conferred the prestigious 58th Jnanpith Award for exceptional lifelong literary excellence?
options: Akkitham Achuthan Namboothiri and Krishna Sobti
questions.explanation: The 58th Jnanpith Award Selection Board awarded Sanskrit polymath and spiritual guru Jagadguru Rambhadracharya alongside eminent poet and filmmaker Gulzar (Sampooran Singh Kalra).

questions.q: Who serves as the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) of India, functioning as the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee?
options: Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh
questions.explanation: General Anil Chauhan serves as India's second Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), heading the Department of Military Affairs (DMA) under the Ministry of Defence.

questions.q: The world's highest railway arch bridge, rising 359 meters above the river bed on the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL), spans across which river?
questions.explanation: The Chenab Rail Bridge in Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir stands at an elevation of 359 meters above the Chenab riverbed (35 meters taller than the Eiffel Tower).

questions.q: India's indigenously developed semiconductor fabrication plant approved under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) is being established in which state by Tata Electronics in partnership with Powerchip (PSMC)?
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved India's first commercial semiconductor fabrication unit in Dholera, Gujarat, spearheaded by Tata Electronics and Taiwan's PSMC with a ₹91,000 crore investment.

questions.q: In the Global Innovation Index (GII) published annually by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), India's ranking has ascended into which tier?
questions.explanation: India rose to 39th position out of 133 economies in the Global Innovation Index (GII), retaining its top position in Central and Southern Asia and among lower-middle-income economies.

questions.q: Under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) approved by the Union Cabinet, which site was selected for setting up India's first commercial semiconductor fabrication facility (Fab) by Tata Electronics and Powerchip (PSMC)?
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved the establishment of India's first commercial semiconductor wafer fabrication facility by Tata Electronics in partnership with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp (PSMC) at Dholera Special Investment Region (SIR) in Gujarat with an investment of ₹91,000 crore.

questions.q: What is the name of the female humanoid robot developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) to fly aboard uncrewed test missions of the Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme?
questions.explanation: Vyommitra ("Space Friend") is a half-humanoid robot developed by ISRO. Equipped with artificial intelligence and speech capabilities, she is programmed to monitor environmental parameters, operate control panels, and simulate human physiological responses during Gaganyaan uncrewed test flights.

questions.q: Under the PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana launched with an outlay of ₹75,021 crore, how many units of free electricity per month are targeted for 1 crore beneficiary households?
questions.explanation: PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana aims to install rooftop solar panels across 1 crore households in India, providing up to 300 units of free electricity per month, generating surplus power for DISCOMs, and reducing annual carbon emissions by 720 million tonnes.

questions.q: The Union Cabinet approved the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) for Central Government employees. What percentage of the average basic pay drawn in the last 12 months is guaranteed as assured pension for qualifying service of minimum 25 years?
questions.explanation: The Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) guarantees an assured pension of 50% of the average basic pay drawn over the last 12 months prior to superannuation for employees with a minimum qualifying service of 25 years. It also provides an assured minimum pension of ₹10,000 per month for service of at least 10 years.

questions.q: Under India's Deep Ocean Mission, what is the name of the indigenously developed manned submersible designed to carry three scientists to an ocean depth of 6,000 meters?
questions.explanation: MATSYA 6000 is an indigenously developed human submersible vehicle developed by the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT) under the Deep Ocean Mission (Samudrayaan), engineered with a titanium alloy personnel sphere to explore hydrothermal vents and polymetallic nodules at 6,000 meters depth.

questions.q: The Union Cabinet approved the continuation and expansion of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY 2.0). How many additional affordable houses were approved for construction across rural and urban sectors?
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi approved government assistance for constructing an additional 3 crore houses under PMAY—comprising 2 crore houses in rural areas (PMAY-Gramin) and 1 crore houses in urban areas (PMAY-Urban 2.0).

questions.q: Which second indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN) was commissioned into the Indian Navy at Visakhapatnam, strengthening India's strategic nuclear triad?
questions.explanation: INS Arighaat, India's second indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN) built under the Advanced Technology Vessel (ATV) project, was commissioned into the Indian Navy at Visakhapatnam by Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh, reinforcing India's sea-based nuclear deterrence.

questions.q: The Union Cabinet approved the Digital Agriculture Mission with an outlay of ₹2,817 crore. Which core digital public infrastructure component builds a federated registry of farmers linked to land records?
questions.explanation: AgriStack is the foundation of the Digital Agriculture Mission, providing digital public infrastructure comprising Farmer Registry, Geo-referenced Village Land Maps, and Crop Sown Registry to deliver seamless credit, crop insurance, and minimum support price services.

questions.q: Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, what is the acronym of the flagship financial incentive programme designed to domesticate electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production?
questions.explanation: SIGHT stands for Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition. With an allocation of over ₹17,490 crore, it provides direct financial incentives for domestic electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production capacity in India.

questions.q: The Department of Telecommunications launched the Bharat 6G Alliance under the "Bharat 6G Vision" document. What is the target year set by the government for nationwide 6G leadership and commercial deployment?
questions.explanation: The Bharat 6G Vision document, released by the Prime Minister, establishes an apex technology roadmap for India to be a global front-runner in 6G wireless communication technology by 2030, anchored by the Bharat 6G Alliance and indigenous patent development.

questions.q: What is the full title of the BioE3 Policy approved by the Union Cabinet to spearhead a sustainable green bio-economy transition in India?
options: Bio-safety for Ecosystems, Earth and Energy
Biomass for Energy, Ecology and Exports
Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment

A massive subterranean Buddhist vihara complex
The world's earliest copper smelting blast furnace
